table.caption: Four invented cities (invented data for practice). Global firms: number of the world's 500 largest companies with headquarters in the city.

cities-globalization-s2.title: How one shipment of phones gets made
cities-globalization-s2.text: Invented passage for practice, 2026. A company headquartered in a world city signs a contract with a factory in Viet Nam to build two million phones. The money is lent by a bank in London. A law firm in New York checks the contract, and both sides sign it by video call in under an hour. An advertising agency in Tokyo plans the launch. A port company in Singapore books the ships. The factory workers in Viet Nam never meet any of these people, but their hours depend on decisions made in those offices.

items.q: Based on the table, which city most likely ranks highest as a world city?
options: City P
City Q
City R
City S

why.correct: City P leads on every measure of global function: headquarters, international flights and foreign banks. World city rank comes from these links, not from population.
options: Right: City P has the most global functions.
City Q has the most people but few global functions.
City R is well connected but has fewer of each than City P.
City S has the fewest global links on every measure.

items.q: City Q has the largest population but few global firms and foreign banks. What does City Q show?
options: A city's rank in the hierarchy is set by its population
Large cities grow by attracting foreign banks
Small cities like City S are usually world cities
A very large city may have little global reach

why.correct: City Q has 22 million people, so it is very large, yet it has few of the global functions that make a world city.
options: City Q is the largest but not the highest-ranked, so population does not set rank.
The table does not show how cities grow; City Q is large with few foreign banks.
City S has almost no global functions.
Right: size and global function are different things.

items.q: Which question could the table NOT answer?
options: Which city has the most foreign bank offices
Which city has the most people
Which cities trade most with each other
Which city has the most international flights

why.correct: The table gives totals for each city, but no flows between pairs of cities, so it cannot show which cities are most linked to each other.
options: The table gives foreign bank offices for each city.
The table gives population for each city.
Right: the table shows no links between pairs of cities.
The table gives international flights for each city.

items.q: City S is the capital of a small country and runs its national government. Where does City S most likely sit in the urban hierarchy?
options: At the world city level
At the national level
At the level of a major regional hub
Below the level of a market town

why.correct: City S leads its own country but has almost no global firms or flights, so it fits the national level.
options: It has no global headquarters and few international flights.
Right: it leads one country but has little global reach.
It has too few foreign banks and flights to link a world region.
As a capital it ranks above market towns.

items.q: Which detail in the passage shows time-space compression?
options: Both sides sign the contract by video call in under an hour
The factory builds two million phones
The factory workers do not meet the people who decide their hours
The ships are booked by a port company

why.correct: Time-space compression is the shrinking of the time it takes to connect distant places. A deal across continents in under an hour shows it.
options: Right: fast links make distance matter less.
The size of an order says nothing about how fast places connect.
Never meeting shows distance between workers and bosses, not faster links.
Booking ships is a task, not a change in how fast places connect.

items.q: What does the passage suggest about the role of world cities in globalization?
options: Factories decide where the world's money is lent
World cities make most of the goods that are traded
Globalization reduces the importance of cities
Decisions made in a few linked cities shape work in distant places

why.correct: The lending, legal work, advertising and shipping decisions are all made in world cities, and they set the hours of workers far away.
options: In the passage, the bank in London lends the money, not the factory.
In the passage, the phones are made in Viet Nam; the world cities provide decisions and services.
The passage shows cities at the center of the process.
Right: world cities are command centers in a global network.

items.q: Which pair of scales does the passage link?
options: National laws and the prices of farm goods in one region
Local elections and the national borders they shape
Global decisions and local effects
Regional weather patterns and global shipping costs

why.correct: Firms and banks in world cities act at the global scale; the result is felt at the local scale, in the hours of one factory.
options: The passage mentions no national laws or farm prices.
The passage mentions no elections or borders.
Right: the passage ties global decisions to local outcomes.
The passage mentions no weather.

items.q: Which of these is the best sign that a city is a world city?
options: More than 20 million people live in it
Many large firms run their worldwide business from it
It is the oldest city in its country
It covers more land than any other city in its region

why.correct: A world city is defined by its global functions: headquarters, finance, media and links.
options: That defines a metacity, which is about population.
Right: global command functions make a world city.
Age does not give a city global functions.
Area does not give a city global functions.

items.q: In the 2024 GaWC ranking, London and New York were the two most connected cities. Which best explains their rank?
options: They host the most offices of global finance, law and advertising firms
They are the two largest cities in the world by population
They are the capitals of the two largest countries by area
They have the most factories of any cities

why.correct: GaWC measured offices of firms that sell finance, law, accounting, consulting and advertising to other firms. London and New York have the most of these links.
options: Right: global business services set the ranking.
Neither is among the very largest cities by population in 2025 (UN DESA).
New York is not a capital, and neither country is the largest by area.
The ranking does not count factories.

items.q: A new kind of mobile payment appears first in Shanghai and Singapore, then in other large Asian cities, and years later in small towns. Which idea explains this path?
options: Contagious diffusion from village to village
Relocation diffusion by migrants leaving cities
Distance decay from the equator
Hierarchical diffusion down the urban hierarchy

why.correct: The idea moves from the top of the urban hierarchy down to smaller places, skipping the space between: hierarchical diffusion.
options: Contagious diffusion spreads to nearby places first, not to the biggest cities.
Nothing in the path shows people moving.
Distance decay is about distance between places, not from the equator.
Right: it spreads down the ladder of cities.

items.q: Many highly paid finance workers move into a world city. Which effect inside the city is most likely?
options: Rents fall because builders put up more homes than the city needs
The city loses many of its airport links to other world cities
Housing costs rise and low-wage workers move out
Fewer jobs are created for cleaners, cooks and bus drivers in the city

why.correct: High-paid newcomers bid up housing, so costs rise and lower-paid workers are pushed toward the edge. Every link matters: more money chasing homes, higher prices, longer commutes.
options: More demand pushes rents up, not down.
Finance workers add to demand for flights.
Right: global money raises local housing costs.
High earners create demand for service jobs, not fewer of them.

items.q: A bank board in London decides to stop lending to a textile company, and a factory in Dhaka cuts 2,000 jobs. Which statement describes the scales involved?
options: A decision at the local scale has an effect at the global scale
A decision at the global scale has an effect at the local scale
Both the decision and the effect are at the national scale
The scale is unclear unless a map of the bank and factory is given

why.correct: The bank acts in the world economy, a global-scale decision; the job losses fall on one factory, a local-scale effect.
options: This reverses the direction: the decision is global and the effect local.
Right: global decision, local effect.
The decision crosses countries, so it is not national.
The scale of a process can be named from what it reaches.

items.q: Put these levels of the urban hierarchy in order, from the top to the base.
options: World city
Major city linking a world region
National capital
Regional city
Small market town

why.correct: Each level serves a larger area than the one below: world, world region, country, part of a country, nearby farms.

items.q: Build the urban hierarchy for Kenya and the world: place each city at its level, top to bottom.

model.title: The urban hierarchy, top to bottom

slips.why: Nairobi leads Kenya, a national role; Johannesburg hosts offices for much of southern Africa, a wider area.

why.correct: London serves the world, Johannesburg a world region, Nairobi one country and Kisumu part of a country. An edge city is a part of a metro area, not a level of the hierarchy.

items.q: Build an explanation of why a named city ranks high in the urban hierarchy.

specific.model: Singapore ranks high because many global banks and shipping firms run their Asian business from it, so its decisions reach factories and ports across Southeast Asia.

place.label: City
options: Singapore
A big city

why.1: Name a real city; a vague answer earns nothing.

cause.label: Function
options: many global banks and shipping firms run their Asian business from it
it has a very large population

why.1: Population makes a megacity; global functions make a world city.

effect.label: Reach
options: its decisions reach factories and ports across Southeast Asia
it has more farmland than nearby cities

why.1: Farmland is not what gives a city reach in the hierarchy.

why.correct: A full explanation names the city, the global function and how that function gives it reach.
